column1: # Beta-lactam enzyme family nomenclature for the pilot-100 analysis.
# WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS
# AMRFinderPlus reports a single Class value of `BETA-LACTAM` for every
# beta-lactamase, with Subclass values of CEPHALOSPORIN, BETA-LACTAM or
# CARBAPENEM. It does NOT distinguish extended-spectrum beta-lactamases
# (ESBL) from metallo-beta-lactamases (MBL). Verified on the
# AMRFinderPlus database version 2026-08-07.1 used for this pilot.
# So the ESBL / MBL / other-beta-lactamase split cannot be read out of the
# AMRFinderPlus class and subclass fields. It has to come from somewhere,
# and the honest place for it is a reviewable, editable data table like this
# one - not buried in an analysis script.
# PROVENANCE AND LIMITS - read before using these labels
# These families follow standard, widely used beta-lactamase enzyme-family
# nomenclature (the same families used by CARD, AMRFinder and the wider
# literature). They are a NAME-BASED classification, not an experimental
# result. Nothing here was measured: no isolate was phenotyped for ESBL or
# MBL activity, and no enzyme characterisation was performed.
# Consequences:
#   * a gene in the MBL family is reported as an MBL *by nomenclature*;
#   * a gene in the ESBL family is reported as an ESBL *by nomenclature*;
#   * neither label says the enzyme is expressed in that isolate;
#   * neither label says the isolate is clinically resistant to that class;
#   * an unlisted beta-lactamase is reported as "Other beta-lactamase", never
#     guessed into ESBL or MBL.
# Gene matching is by exact element symbol. `blaVIM` matches `blaVIM-6`
# because the table entry carries an explicit wildcard-free prefix and the
# matcher strips a trailing `-\d+` allele number before comparing.
# family       : the functional category reported
# gene_prefix  : element-symbol prefix to match, before allele-number stripping
# basis        : nomenclature | amrfinder_subclass
# notes        : the caveat carried into the report
